title: Move Your Subnet Spreadsheet into Micetro in One Paste

cta.text: Bring your spreadsheet to a Micetro evaluation

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Move Your Subnet Spreadsheet into Micetro in One Paste".
Story: From Spreadsheet to Managed Networks in One Paste
Most teams track their subnets and who owns them in a spreadsheet, because moving them into a real tool sounds like weeks of data entry. Watch BlueCat Micetro take that spreadsheet in with one paste, then attach owners to individual addresses through the same wizard. About 4 minutes.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
14 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element:
1. Your subnets live in a spreadsheet, with no single place to manage them. Micetro changes that, starting with the spreadsheet you already have.
2. Import is a single item in the Action menu on the networks list.
3. The same wizard imports networks, IP addresses, devices and DHCP reservations, so a whole spreadsheet can come across in stages. First up: networks.
4. Copy the cells from the spreadsheet and paste them in. One header row, six subnets, no conversion step.
5. Before anything is written, Micetro shows how it read every column: range, title, description and location. Mistakes would be flagged here.
6. Import, and the whole list is created in one action. Every row gets its own check mark.
7. The import worked: the spreadsheet's networks are now managed in Micetro.
8. Quick filter jumps straight to the networks you just imported: all six are there, ready to use.
9. Inside Chicago Users: its 32 addresses, ready for the details the spreadsheet holds about each one.
10. Address-level details such as owners come in through the same wizard: an address and a responsible person per line.
11. The same preview, the same safety check, before anything changes.
12. Three owners imported in one action.
13. Refresh the list and three addresses flip to Assigned: the owners from the spreadsheet are now attached to them.
14. With the side panels out of the way, the Responsible Person column shows who owns each address: Priya, Marcus and Dana. The spreadsheet's knowledge now lives in the system, where everyone can see it.
Close: Your spreadsheet becomes governed network data in one paste, with no conversion step.
End with a call to action: Bring your spreadsheet to a Micetro evaluation.
